title: Priming Panopticon — deploy journal & pinning heuristics
content:
Purpose and quick summary

Quick brain-dump for a release pattern experiment: run a small, persistent "priming" cohort alongside the usual canary and warmup cohorts to catch cold-cache regressions and subtle quality regressions introduced by quantization/kv changes. This is less about immediate rollback and more about surfacing slow drift that standard canaries miss.

Notes to self — context: why this exists
- We keep hitting small but steady increases in tail-latency and occasional hallucination spikes after model flips that only appear after tens of minutes of real traffic.
- Hypothesis: prefix caching + tiny client distribution differences mean the canary (short-lived, tiny % traffic) isn't exercising the latent hot-paths.
- Goal: create a low-volume, always-on cohort that mimics production long-lived sessions and long-context behavior.

Cohort design (priming cohort) — quick sketch
- Size: 0.2% of traffic or 3–5 steady client IDs (whichever yields more realistic session length).
- Target tenants: pick 1 paid customer + synthetic session generator with long-history prompts.
- Session type: long-lived conversations (avg tokens/session target 3–6k), interleaved with short queries.
- Traffic shaping: route only authenticated sessions (so we can persist KV caches per-session).
- Lifespan: cohort should persist across deploys for at least 24–72 hours to observe accumulation effects.

Priming actions and instrumentation
- Cache telemetry: track per-session KV cache hit-rate, avg cached prefix size, and eviction rate.
- Quality telemetry: attach prompt-set regression tests every 30m for this cohort (short evals with fuzzed user messages).
- Latency telemetry: track p50/p95/p99 for first token vs steady-state tokens per session.
- Memory / GPU metrics: watch per-worker KV memory growth and global kv-eviction spikes.
- Alerts: synthetic-session-priming-quality-drop (>5% on ground-truth prompts) => P2.

Pinning semantics & rollout interactions (hosted / dedicated / private)
- Pin semantics: when we 'pin' a tenant to old-model we must also pin to the old kv-config/quantization profile. Pinning only model version risks introducing cache-format mismatch.
- Dedicated: communicate that pin = model + runtime-config (kv-version, quant-profile). Provide immediate toggle in tenant admin page.
- Private: include migration script alongside release: kv-format-migrate.sh; need ops signoff for in-place migration.

Warmup sequence (experiment variant A/B)
- Variant A: warmup-first then canary. Steps:
  1) deploy with zero traffic routing.
  2) kick generator that replays warmup traces to populate KV on allocated workers (8–12 minutes wall-time per worker ideally).
  3) enable priming cohort (0.2% persistent) for 1 hour.
  4) open canary to 1% for 30 minutes.
- Variant B: canary-first then warmup (fast check then fill caches). Notes: risk of canary missing cache-driven regressions.

Checklist before flip (quick checklist to pin in release ticket)
- [ ] Release notes include kv/quant-profile changes and migration hints.
- [ ] Rollout page: list tenants pre-approved for priming cohort.
- [ ] Observability queries in console: add priming cohort dashboards (query names below).
- [ ] Canary runbook updated with priming cohort gating step.
- [ ] Admin toggle for pin exposed and tested.

Quick queries & dashboards to create (names for console)
- priming.sessions.active_count
- priming.kv.hit_rate.1h
- priming.latency.first_token.p99
- priming.quality.regression_rate.30m

Rollback & escape hatches
- Immediate pinback: route tenant to last-stable image + last-stable-runtime-config. This should preserve old kv-format.
- Fast-eviction: if kv memory climbs >20% over baseline, evict priming cohort (temporarily stop routing).
- Graceful degrade: fallback model to smaller quantized variant when worker queue depth > 80%.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to iterate)
- How to share priming cohort across regions without duplicating sensitive tenant data? (Option: synthetic replay that mirrors tenant traces.)
- Is 0.2% the right size? Need simulation run against last 30 days of production traffic (see PLAT-4721).
- How to make priming-cohort selection reproducible for customers (so they can opt-in)?
- Confirm whether Dedicated autoscaler respects priming-cohort worker warmup quotas (ask infra team).

Edge cases observed in preliminary runs (field notes)
- Observed: priming sessions occasionally keep KV entries for >18 hours and cause high mem churn on a single worker after a dev flip that changed embedding dims. Investigate embedding shape compatibility in migration path.
- Observed: small QoS blip when priming cohort shares workers with high-throughput tenants. Consider worker affinity flags.

Notes-to-self (style = choppy, action-oriented)
- Add clear note in PR template: "Does this change affect kv serialization or runtime config? If yes, include migration plan."
- Create a tiny harness that replays 5 long sessions with randomized interruptions to simulate real customers (use measurables: token cadence, history size).
- Coordinate with cs-eng for two tenants willing to be priming participants for 48–72h.

References & links
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284 (runtime kv changes)
- Jira: PLAT-4721 (priming cohort design epic)
- Slack thread: #release-warmup (C01XYZ thread timestamped above)

Run notes (short log)
- 2025-01-10: prototype priming harness ran in staging for 6h. Observed 2% increase in p99 for steady-state tokens only when cache miss > 30%.
- 2025-01-24: toggled priming cohort in EU1 for 12h. No consumer-visible errors but saw kv-eviction spikes at 03:10 UTC (investigate garbage collection thresholds).

If I forget everything: single sentence summary
- Keep a tiny, always-on cohort that mirrors long-lived sessions; treat pin as model+runtime-config; warmup before canary when KV/serialization changes to reduce silent regressions.

End of note.

(If this lands in a formal runbook, condense to steps + exact queries + owners.)
